test.title: A historical place you have visited

document.cue: Describe a historical place you have visited.

text: The historical place I'd like to describe is the Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi in the city of Turkistan, in the south of Kazakhstan. I visited it two years ago on a school trip, and it's still one of the most impressive buildings I've ever seen.

It was built at the end of the fourteenth century on the orders of Timur, to honour a Sufi poet and teacher who lived there two hundred years earlier. What surprised me is that it was never actually finished — you can still see bare brick walls on one side, where the decorative tiles were never added. Since 2003 it's been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Inside, the main hall is enormous and very quiet. Our guide showed us a huge bronze cauldron in the middle, which can hold about three thousand litres of water, and explained that it was used to give water to pilgrims. Outside, the blue domes look almost unreal against the desert sky, especially in the evening light.

I learned how important Turkistan was as a centre of learning and culture on the Silk Road. Before the trip, history was just dates in a textbook for me, but standing in a building that's more than six hundred years old made it feel real and connected to people like me.
I'd love to go back one day and spend more time there.

tips.en: It was never actually finished is a memorable fact.
